options.text: When a patient says they are afraid of a procedure, I do not downplay the feeling; instead, I find out what worries them most and pass the information to the team to support preparation.

If family members express wishes that conflict with each other, I keep the patient's will and the goals of care as the starting point of the discussion and, if necessary, guide them to a joint care meeting.
For continuity of care, it is essential that unclear observations are documented openly but without exaggeration so that they can be monitored reliably during the following shifts.
When we agree on follow-up care among several parties, I make sure before the end of my shift that responsibilities, schedules, and criteria for making contact have been documented unambiguously.
